what am I looking at?

The price — EUR/USD: euros priced in dollars. 1.1000 → 1.1050 is +50 pips. Long = you win when it rises; short = you win when it falls.

20 / 100-day avg — the average price of the last 20 / 100 sessions. Price above a rising average = uptrend. Price crossing an average is momentum changing.

US dollar, flipped — the dollar index, drawn upside-down so it normally moves in the same direction as the price line (a stronger dollar pushes EUR/USD down). When the two lines split apart, something euro-side is driving instead.

last 5 / 20 days — net pips over the last 5 / 20 sessions: recent momentum, short and medium.

how wild — how violently it's been moving lately. Wild = bigger swings both ways.

The CSV export also logs two numbers not shown here: the 60-day correlation with the flipped dollar, and the 20-session change in the US 10-year yield.

Hit rate vs the coin-flip zone
·
how to play & data sources

Each round drops you at a hidden date in the past. 1D plays daily bars (2007–2026, with the dollar-mirror pane); 1H plays hourly bars. WAIT walks the tape one bar while you stay flat — wait as long as you like. LONG / SHORT enters at the current bar; ride with NEXT SESSION and book with EXIT whenever you choose — there is no time limit, a position only auto-books if the data itself ends. Pass ends the round without a trade. Dates unseal only when the round ends.

The coin-flip zone is the 95% range a pure guesser's hit rate lands in after the same number of trades. Every round logs its date, your action, sessions waited and held, the result in pips, and the context you saw — export the CSV and study your own tape.

Prices: ECB daily EUR/USD fixes (1D); HistData.com minute data resampled to hourly (1H). Dollar mirror: UUP. Yields: US 10-year constant maturity.
